source: Maybe not that exactly. But I think this spirit told Hamlet something which drove him mad.
All I can tell you is this: Strange things are afoot in Elsinore.
That being said, with everything that's transpired lately, I think Hamlet, too, has changed.
He's seriously considering his own ascension to the throne.
I've been speaking with him, and he seems more clear-minded now than I've ever seen him before.
Give it time. His mood may lift on its own.
Come to think of it, Ophelia... have you ever read the report of the late King Hamlet's death?
It's shelved in the gallery. If you were to, er, peruse it...
Perhaps you'd better understand what causes Hamlet's ailment.
Regardless, if Hamlet is planning something, then the next few days will force his hand.
Given your history with him, you of all people should know he doesn't keep secrets very well.
Hamlet is acting incredibly strangely, and I'm worried.
I think he's been going through an incredible darkness.
I finally spoke to him, you know. First time in years. And it was illuminating.
I do not think there will be a time when Hamlet is no threat to us.
But I think he and I reached a kind of understanding. At least for now.
I hope he troubles you no more. The monsters in his mind are loud.
Did he threaten you?
No, no. It was nothing like that. Just being a fool.
Well, that's not strange, is it? That's how he always is with you lately. A lovesick idiot, like a dog that comes crawling back even after it's been kicked.
On top of that, he's now a betrothed man. He cares little for what's proper. Always has.
This time was different, somehow...
Are you concerned?
Possibly. He came into my room, partially-clothed, raving about nothing in particular.
A-and you didn't tell me that first?
Then I must stay. To keep watch. Until this fit of his lifts.
I'd better not go to Paris. Not yet, at least. I'll ask the docksmen to hold in the bay.
Father will be furious, of course.
(If he stays, things will change.)
That would make me feel much better.
Well, then that settles it. You're more important than any trip, Ophelia.
I'll stay here and keep an eye on the situation.
You're certain you want to stay just because Hamlet might do something inappropriate?
You don't understand what men are capable of. That's a blessing. I promise you.
Maybe not, but I know what Hamlet is capable of. He doesn't frighten me.
This is your one opportunity to go to Paris. Take it. Please.
All right. If you insist. But write me often. I want to hear when things improve.
He's going to pay for this. First everything else, now he comes after my sister?
I'll kill him. I'll tear him down until he regrets leaving Wittenberg.
Hamlet is acting very strangely. Do you know the cause?
Given current circumstances, I can't discuss it, my lady.
Needless to say, very soon he won't be causing you any more pain. I'll make certain of that.
Ah. I was afraid of this.
No. Nothing. It's nothing.
Where is your father? Have you told him about this? I can have a man assigned to your hall in case the Prince should bother you further.
I can have a man assigned to your hall in case the Prince should bother you further.
It's quite all right. He's not a danger to me. Not yet, anyway.
... Lady Ophelia, before you depart...
Have you been to the gallery? There is a certain tome there... filled with the lives and deaths of royal men and women.
The entry on King Hamlet may be of particular interest to you, if you're concerned about the Prince's well-being.
Why the secrecy, Bernardo?
Would that I could say, my lady. But I have promised my silence.
Of course. As do you.
The ghost. His father's spirit.
I suppose that would weigh on him.
I could see in his face that it was... well... something broke in him. I don't know what.
But even I am afraid of it, my lady.
Hamlet is acting incredibly strangely, and I'm not sure why.
I am not surprised. And now the former brat is to be our king.
He may seem determined, but his mind is no less fractured.
His insolent attitude weighs on my lady's consciousness like a fat stone!
A burden, a disgrace, nothing but a nuisance... my poor Gerta must deal with him day and night.
The boy needs a firm hand, and gets none!
The last noble who suffered from such a broken mind put everyone through even more strife before her death.
I hope his end is less... painful.
What do you mean by... the last noble?
Lady Astrid. You did not know of her?
No, no. I suppose you wouldn't... it happened long before you were born.
Those of us with eyes in our heads know better than to speak of her. But visit the gallery...
Yes, the gallery. Not all traces of a woman can be removed, especially one with blue blood.
The gallery...
You mean Queen Astrid.
Those of us with eyes in our heads know better than to speak of her. But... not all traces of a woman can be removed, especially one with blue blood.
Some others around here still know the tale to tell it, if only in whispers. It happened several years before I came to Elsinore.
Hamlet is acting incredibly strangely. Do you know why?
A-ah-- it must be because of-- well, I heard the story about what happened with your father.
We all know about what Hamlet did.
Ophelia, are you all right?
You really can't imagine? You left him in pieces. Everyone knows it.
Although it looks like I, as his future wife, get to be the one to pick those pieces up. I am obviously just giddy with joy.
This was beyond any lingering feelings he might have for me. This was madness. He was wild-eyed, raving.
Oh. That is interesting, then.
You know, I overheard the most interesting argument before your brother left for Paris...
He and Hamlet were shouting at each other in the hallway. I could hear it from my chambers. The walls were practically shaking.
Your brother said he was going to write your father a letter, and if the problem wasn't resolved by his return, he'd strangle Hamlet to death.
He does seem to threaten to strangle Hamlet a lot, though.
Either way, perhaps that letter's what's put Hamlet into such a fit. Were I you, I'd have a look, 'Feely.
Hamlet came into my room and accosted me, seemingly mad. Do you know why?
Ophelia, horrid things're afoot here.
Like what?
...I've been commanded not t'say.
If yeh follow Hamlet, he may lead yeh to the answer himself.
It's strange. Th'last time somethin' like this happened... well...
It didn' end well for poor Queen Astrid.
Queen Astrid?
I know I've heard of that name before, but... why do you say that?
... I shouldn't 'a said anything.
Still, I pray that Hamlet's state doesn' get any worse. For all of our sakes.
This is so unlike him.
Rosie and I really ought to talk some sense into him.
Not in the slightest! He's an iron fortress, that one.
What makes you take such an interest in his state, Ophelia?
I seem to be a target of his mood swings. I'd prefer not to be, so I'm trying to find the root cause.
Hmm. I think I need to speak with my compatriot Rosie here. In private.
Oh, Hamlet!
He was never like this at school...
We're as clueless as you. We tried to talk with him, but...
No luck at all.
That does seem prudent. I'll speak with Guilda when I've a free moment.
What do you know about the ghost haunting the walls of Elsinore?
Such a delightful little pawn to have in the game, that one.
Consider him the audience to our match, if you will.
A match without anyone to cheer is no fun at all!
He's not cheering for you.
He'll cheer for whomever I tell him to. He is a puppet of mine.
Don't you understand that yet?
And if ever he becomes an annoyance...
Then away he'll go!
That he's been buried deep forever now.
Were you hoping he would make a glorious return? A wondrous comeback to save you?
No. He's dead and gone, lady.
I have written his grim conclusion.
A multitude of things. For what purpose are you eager to track down this spirit?
If this is what's causing Hamlet's madness, then this is what's causing him to kill my father.
And... if... I, myself, have become a supernatural oddity, then perhaps finding another will pave the way forward.
Hmm. Yes. I follow.
Then heed this: to track down the father, you must go through the son.
Once his mind has been swayed, follow it to its natural conclusion.
Your Highness, Hamlet claimed that he saw the ghost of his late father.
Well, it matters little now.
They say all are reunited in death. Perhaps my brother and Hamlet are together.
Ghosts, now?
I know the boy is still upset about my brother's unfortunate death, but if he's saying things like that...
Where did you get this information?
I... overheard it. From the prince himself. Bernardo and Horatio also have seen it.
I see. I'll have to have a word with them, I think.
Thank you for coming to me, Ophelia. Your father will be proud.
Thank you for coming to me, Ophelia. Your father would have been proud.
Did Hamlet actually see his father's ghost?
Yes. I think... that's part of why he died.
I saw the spirit with my own eyes. Hamlet had a conversation with it. And after that, nothing was the same. He was changed.
I spoke with it, too.
What does it want, then?
Revenge. As spirits always do, I imagine.
I see. I always had my suspicions about the way the King passed. Now, it seems, they've been confirmed.
Not that there's much a poor sod like me can do about that.
How can I meet it myself? Perhaps—speak to it?
Ah. It would only speak to Hamlet. I tried to get its attention, but it didn't seem to care much for me.
And with him gone, I wonder if it has any cause to appear at all now.
Oh! So he told you about it after all? I'm glad.
You know, I'm relieved you've learned about it. I do so hate keeping secrets.
Yes, he did, and we were rather shocked when we saw it. If the others hadn't seen it as well, surely I would have thought I was losing my mind.
We were up on the walls. It wore the same armor as His Majesty did when he fought the King of Norway years ago.
Ah. It'll only speak to Hamlet, you know. I tried to get its attention, but it didn't seem to care much for me.
